data.title: Far South violence continues, but reduced
data.description: Dissidents struck again in the southern border province of Pattani late Sunday night, bombing and burning a municipal office, in the wake of a storm of violence in the far South on Saturday night.

data.title: Malaysians advised to defer non-essential trips to south Thailand
data.description: Malaysians have been strongly advised by their own police to put on hold non-essential visits to southern Thailand as bombings, shootings and arson continue to plague the region.

data.title: Exhausted flood-relief volunteer dies in Nan
data.description: A volunteer relief worker was found dead in his hotel room in flood-devastated Nan province on Monday morning, after working tirelessly to help flood victims in this northern province throughout the last week.

data.title: Contract ready for bridge to Koh Lanta, to open in 3 years
data.description: The contract for a road bridge connecting mainland Krabi with Koh Lanta island will be signed next Monday, with the planned opening in 2029, Transport Minister Phiphat Ratchakitprakarn said.

data.title: EC outlines hurdles in Senate election fraud case
data.description: <p>The Election Commission (EC) can refer alleged fraud cases from the 2024 Senate election to the Supreme Court only when three specific legal conditions are met, EC Secretary-General Sawaeng Boonmee says.</p>

data.title: Clear rules on data centres needed
data.description: <p>The government needs to quickly establish clear standards and operating guidelines for data centres to manage the sector's growing demands on resources and the environment, says Surasak Boonrueang, an associate professor at Thammasat University's Natural Resources and Environmental Law Centre.</p>

data.title: Tourist rescued off Nai Thon beach
data.description: PHUKET: A foreign tourist was rescued at Nai Thon Beach in Phuket after ignoring lifeguards' warnings and entering the sea despite a red flag.

data.title: Tourism hub eyed for state land
data.description: PHANGNGA: The Transport Ministry is exploring a 765-rai development in Takua Thung district, with plans for hotels and wellness centres alongside tourism and service activities.

data.title: Democrats seek witness  protection in exam case
data.description: <p>The Democrat Party will petition the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC) on Monday for clear guidelines to protect witnesses in the local government examination fraud case.</p>

data.title: 2nd day of M6 trial sees 15k vehicles
data.description: <p>Traffic on the new section of the M6 motorway rose sharply on its second day of trials, with more than 15,500 vehicles using the route.</p>

data.title: Institute vows legal action in bribery case
data.description: <p>Issara Sereewatthanawut, secretary-general of the King Prajadhipok's Institute, has pledged to take legal action over allegations that payments were sought for admission to its executive training programme.</p>

data.title: Knives seized at late-night gathering
data.description: <p>Police in Nakhon Ratchasima detained 16 youths and arrested three men after breaking up a late-night gathering called to prepare for a street fight.</p>

data.title: Nida poll finds doubts over Anutin govt survival
data.description: <p>Almost 40% of respondents in a recent Nida Poll believe Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul's government will not survive its current challenges, with local government examination fraud cited as its biggest problem.</p>

data.title: Sombat faces sex assault allegations
data.description: <p>Political activist Sombat Boonngamanong is the latest prominent activist to face sexual assault allegations rocking Thailand's pro-democracy movement.</p>

data.title: Army plays down attacks
data.description: <p>A coordinated wave of 51 attacks across Narathiwat, Pattani and Yala may have been launched to discredit state officials and retaliate against a crackdown on illicit trade, Fourth Army Area commander Lt Gen Norathip Phoynok says.</p>

data.title: PM orders rapid cleanup across Nan
data.description: <p>Damaged homes and infrastructure in Nan should be restored within four to five days so residents can return home, said Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, ordering authorities to accelerate flood recovery operations.</p>

data.title: Gun probe finds 'suspect' permits
data.description: <p>A Department of Provincial Administration (Dopa) operation in Phitsanulok has uncovered 2,255 suspicious firearms permits with no corresponding possession licences since 2020, the highest number recorded in Thailand.</p>

data.title: Amnesty law takes effect Monday, excludes lese majeste offences
data.description: The Peaceful Society Promotion Act has been published in the Royal Gazette and will take effect on Monday, granting amnesty for a wide range of political offences committed over the past two decades, but excluding lese majeste cases.

data.title: American faces attempted murder charge after drug-fuelled robbery
data.description: An American man who allegedly stole beer from a convenience store in Bangkok while high on methamphetamine and later slashed a policeman's neck when he tried to arrest him will be charged with attempted murder.

data.title: Southern border rail track closed after being bombed
data.description: NARATHIWAT - An overnight bomb explosion damaged the southern rail track in Rangae district of this southern border province, and it was closed for security checks and repairs, affecting 10 freight and long-haul passenger services.

data.title: Nan flood recovery under way, aid payments prepared
data.description: NAN - Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul on Sunday ordered state agencies to speed up flood recovery, compensation payments and infrastructure repairs in Nan and other flood-affected provinces, while maintaining heightened monitoring for further flooding and landslides during the remainder of the rainy season.

data.title: Tougher parole rules proposed for most-serious offenders
data.description: The Justice Ministry is drafting new rules that would require prisoners sentenced to death or life imprisonment to serve far longer behind bars before becoming eligible for prisoner-classification upgrades, parole or other sentence-reduction benefits.

data.title: Bombings and arson continue in South
data.description: There were 51 violent incidents in the three southernmost border provinces on Saturday night, almost half of them occurring in Narathiwat.

data.title: Dept eyes 74km Suphan Buri-Ayutthaya rail link
data.description: A new 73.8-kilometre railway linking Suphan Buri with Ban Phachi in Ayutthaya is being developed to close a missing link and improve freight connections.

data.title: Opposition gears up for no-confidence debate
data.description: <p>The opposition is stepping up preparations for a no-confidence debate against the government, with the Democrat Party signalling it will scrutinise alleged collusion in the Senate election, the controversial TH-AI Passport project and alleged administrative failures in the Public Health Ministry.</p>

data.title: Raid nets 'illegal weapons' in Phuket
data.description: PHUKET: Police seized 26 firearms and 495 rounds of ammunition in 39 cases during a nine-day crackdown targeting illegal weapons across the province.

data.title: Auckland flights to resume
data.description: Thai Airways International will resume direct flights between Bangkok and Auckland next year.

data.title: Govt pushes Chana estate plan
data.description: <p>The government is preparing to push the Chana industrial estate and second deep-sea port project at the cabinet's upcoming meeting in Songkhla.</p>

data.title: Royal cancer drug Imcranib distributed at four hospitals
data.description: <p>The Public Health Ministry has begun distributing 2,880 boxes of the cancer treatment drug Imcranib to four hospitals, benefiting 215 patients.</p>

data.title: Thailand eyes NZ trade hub role
data.description: <p>Thailand is positioning itself as a regional distribution hub for New Zealand goods while seeking greater investment and cooperation in clean energy and agricultural technology, Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas said.</p>

data.title: CAAT ramps up regional airport upgrade plan
data.description: <p>The Civil Aviation Authority of Thailand (CAAT) is accelerating upgrades to regional airports and the aviation network to accommodate rising air travel, with a focus on safety, readiness and tailored development under its "Small Airports, Not Small Standards" concept.</p>

data.title: Bomb blasts, arson attacks rock Narathiwat, two injured
data.description: A string of unrest occurred at multiple locations in southern border provinces on Saturday night, with explosions and arson attacks damaging vehicles, communication infrastructure and other property. Two people were injured in Narathiwat.

data.title: Veteran activist apologises after sexual assault claims surface
data.description: Veteran activist Somyot Pruksakasemsuk has apologised to a woman who accused him of sexual assault, acknowledging he misunderstood her consent and promising not to repeat such acts.

data.title: Nominee raids extend to three sites in Pattaya
data.description: Officials have raided three locations in Pattaya and seized computers and documents linked to a suspected nominee scheme concealing foreign ownership of land and businesses.

data.title: War weapons from Cambodia seized in Trat
data.description: A smuggling suspect has been arrested and two AK-47 rifles, more than 24,000 rounds of ammunition and other items smuggled from Cambodia seized at a pier in Laem Ngop district of Trat province.
